reading_note: The teaching enumerates four great "kingdoms in the world" — read as four discrete degrees of dominion or governing love that order the natural plane. The arc moves from a general statement that such governing states exist, through their sequential enumeration (first, second, third, fourth), to the closing summation: these four exhaust the modes of rulership at the natural level, and nothing of the same order stands above them. Spiritually, this maps the four registers through which a ruling love organizes natural life — corresponding to the four cardinal states (good of love, truth of that good, truth of faith, work from faith) when read positively, or the four self-loves when read in opposite sense. Heavy lacunae make the assignment of each individual kingdom uncertain; only the structural arc of four-fold rule is secure.
